newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ c/a deficit at yr end rose to 4.2 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: NZ c/a deficit at yr end rose to 4.2 pct of GDP.

text.p: New Zealand's current account deficit as a percentage of GDP grew to 4.2 percent in the year ended December 31, 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.

SNZ said the deficit in the year to September 1996 had been revised down to 3.9 percent of GDP from the previously published 4.6 percent. In the year to December 1995 the deficit was 3.7 percent of GDP.
"The December 1996 ratio is the highest since 5.1 percent in the December 1987 year," SNZ said.

New Zealand's December quarter current account deficit was NZ$1.29 billion, against a revised $1.95 billion deficit in the September quarter and a $0.1 billion deficit in the December quarter of 1995.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected a $1.13 billion quarterly deficit.
In the year to December the deficit was NZ$3.91 billion, against a revised deficit of $3.62 billion in the year to September and a $3.32 billion deficit in the year to December 1995.
Economists had forecast a $4.25 billion annual deficit.
SNZ said that on a seasonally-adjusted basis, the December 1996 quarter deficit was $907 million, an improvement of $105 million over the September quarter deficit.
A $132 million improvement in the seasonally adjusted merchandise trade balance was the major influence on the improved seasonally adjusted current account deficit in the quarter.
In the December quarter, both exports and imports fell, but the fall in imports was larger.
SNZ said a continued fall in the seasonally adjusted invisibles balance for the quarter had dampened the improvement the merchandise balance had on the current account deficit.
It added that the current account balance trend had shown indications of improvement in the last two quarters, compared with the long term deterioration evident since June 1993.
Recent improvements in the trade balance trend were the major influence.
